source.book: The Art and Science of Technical Analysis
source.author: Adam Grimes

conventions: stop and limit entries mechanized as bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; price-level conditions rejected (shift test)

candidates.name: DailyLossLimitSwitch
candidates.quote: Is there a loss level at which you will stop trading for the day/week/month?
candidates.description: Equity lost since the start of the current calendar day (or week/month) exceeds a dollar threshold; blocks new entries and forces flat until the period rolls over. The daily-loss-limit generalization of the existing MonthlyProfitTarget Switch, mirrored onto the loss side and onto a day/week boundary instead of a fixed calendar month.

complexity.reason: needs a design decision for how the day/week/month boundary is detected and how starting equity is captured and held as persistent state across bars; the underlying comparison (equity change since a period start vs. a threshold) is simple once that plumbing exists, exactly as MonthlyProfitTarget already does for a calendar month

notes: Grimes gives no explicit dollar figure; the phrasing is a question the trader must answer for his own plan. dailyLossLimit = 1000 is an arbitrary placeholder default, flagged for calibration by the authoring pass.

MonthlyProfitTarget already gates entries on cumulative equity gain since the start of the calendar month (Switch role, blocks entries, forces flat); this candidate is its mirror image (loss instead of gain) generalized to day/week/month instead of a fixed month boundary.
EquityDrawdownFilter is close but reads a rolling N-bar lookback rather than resetting at a calendar boundary -- a different accessor pattern (variable history vs. a captured period-start value).

candidates.name: TradeCountLimitSwitch
candidates.quote: How many trades a day/week/month will you allow?
candidates.description: The number of entries already taken in the current calendar day (or week/month) reaches a cap; blocks further entries until the period rolls over.
candidates.pseudocode:
// tradesToday counts entries taken since the first bar of the current date
if (date[0] != date[1]) tradesToday = 0
if (ctx.MarketPosition() != 0 and ctx.BarsSinceEntry() == 0) tradesToday = tradesToday + 1
tradesToday >= maxTradesPerDay

complexity.reason: no existing ctx accessor counts entries taken since a period start; TotalTrades (used by LastTradeCooldown) is cumulative since the strategy began, not since the current day/week/month started, so a new persistent counter plus a day-boundary reset would need to be designed

notes: Grimes gives no explicit cap; maxTradesPerDay = 5 is an arbitrary placeholder default, flagged for calibration.

Needs a trade-count-since-period-start accessor that does not currently exist in the corpus; closest existing tool is LastTradeCooldown's use of TotalTrades, which is a lifetime counter, not a per-day/week/month one.

chapter_summary: Chapter 12 covers the road map of trader development, the business/personal requirements for trading as a career, building a business and trading plan, journaling and record keeping, and statistical review of trading results (significance tests, %R standardization, control charts). Almost all of it is career, business-practice, or book-only-statistics material with no bar-level test. The trading-plan checklist buried two operational questions that do reduce to position-state tests -- a period loss limit and a cap on trades per period -- mined as Switch candidates G12-01 (DailyLossLimitSwitch) and G12-02 (TradeCountLimitSwitch); both are graded 'research' because Grimes gives no numeric threshold and the corpus has no existing accessor for equity-since-period-start or trades-since-period-start.
